entries.title: Fresh Components
entries.description: Fresh Components is the legacy component library that was created for the rebranding 'echt vers', hence the name fresh components. The component library was an initiative from tech but never made it across the isle to the design team. The library never became a design system and was inconsistent with the mobile applications. The successor of Fresh Components is Pantry design system.

timeline.description: We will leave AH-Fresh-Components as the component library for customer-facing web-frontends.

entries.title: Bun

timeline.description: Bun is being assessed for use as JavaScript runtime, test runner, package manager and/or build tool in specific projects within CTP.

entries.title: Cypress
entries.description: Cypress is a JavaScript-based end-to-end testing framework that enables developers to write, run, and debug tests for web applications in a fast and reliable manner.

timeline.description: We need a better tool for end-to-end tests because Cypress has some limits. It does not fully support all major browsers, especially WebKit and Firefox. Our CI runs are slower because parallel execution is limited. Tests can be flaky because waiting for elements and keeping test state clean is difficult and leads to false negatives in test runs. Place Cypress on Hold in favor of Playwright addoption, see linked ADR.

entries.title: GitHub Advanced Security
entries.description: GitHub Advanced Security is a suite of security features and tools built into the GitHub platform that helps identify and prevent security vulnerabilities in code. It includes features such as Code Scanning, Secret Scanning, Dependabot alerts, and Security Advisories.

timeline.description: GHAS is the default SAST tooling. Checkmarx to be used for code languages not supported by GHAS (e.g. PL/SQL)

Trial started with GAS as replacement for Checkmarx and adding new features like secret and license scanning. GAS is close/part of our Developer platform giving better integration with our processes and tools

entries.title: Jest
entries.description: Jest is a JavaScript testing framework created by Facebook that works out of the box with zero configuration. It provides built-in features like mocking, code coverage, snapshot testing, and parallel test execution. Jest is widely used for testing JavaScript applications, React components, and Node.js code due to its simplicity and comprehensive feature set.

timeline.description: Jest is an industry standard for JavaScript testing with widespread adoption. It's already used by the majority of teams within our organization, and provides comprehensive features like built-in mocking, coverage, and snapshot testing. This eliminates the need for additional tools while leveraging existing team expertise and abundant community resources. Set to adopt because we should not have additional discussions on the unit and component test framework (with the exception on Vitest for Trial)

entries.title: Material UI
entries.description: Material UI is an open-source React component library that implements Google's Material Design system. It's comprehensive, can be used in production out of the box, and is the standard component library in React Admin. It has broad support from Google as well as the online community. When business user interfaces (BUI’s) are implemented Material UI can be used to delivery value fast.

timeline.description: We will adopt Material UI as a component library for employee-facing web frontends when Pantry EX doesn't meet all requirements.

entries.title: Monorepo

timeline.description: Monorepo is adopted

entries.title: Multi Zones based Micro Frontends
entries.description:
Micro Frontends are an architectural style where independently deliverable frontend applications are composed into a greater whole.

While there are various implementations that satisify the definition of a Micro Frontend, we are proposing a multi-zones approach to Micro Frontends that separate a large application on a domain into smaller applications that each serve a set of paths. This approach is best suited for our specific use cases and constraints.

timeline.description: Multi Zones based Micro Frontends is adopted

entries.title: Pantry CX
entries.description: Pantry design system is a comprehensive collection of instructions, principles and conventions, alongside reusable building blocks in the form of styles, assets, components and templates that can be used to create consistent digital products at scale. The system covers both the design process and code implementation. Customer Experience (CX) focuses on customer facing frontend applications.

timeline.description: We will adopt Pantry as a design system for all customer-facing web frontends.

entries.title: SCSS - CSS preprocessor
entries.description: SCSS (Sassy CSS) is a popular CSS preprocessor that extends the capabilities of standard CSS by introducing features like variables, nesting, and mixins. It enables developers to write more maintainable and modular stylesheets, which can be especially beneficial in large-scale React applications. Adopting SCSS as the styling technology aims to streamline the development process and enhance the maintainability of the UI codebase.

timeline.description: We will adopt SCSS as the styling method of React components.

entries.title: Turborepo
entries.description: When using the monorepo software development strategy, CI/CD pipelines of projects can perform slowely when the repositories grow in size over time. Turborepo can efficientily cache and execute, only the pipeline steps related to changes.

timeline.description: Turborepo is adopted.
